chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the woman who menstruates once every three months, how should she count her waiting period? He said: 'She waits for the equivalent of her regular menstruation period when she was regular, so let her count three menstrual periods, then let her marry if she wishes.'

As for what was narrated - Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Yazid ibn Ishaq from Harun ibn Hamza from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) - regarding a woman who was divorced and had reached an advanced age, she had one menstruation, then her menstruation ceased, he said: 'She counts the one menstruation and two following months, for she has despaired of menstruation.'

We interpret this report as applying to the one who despairs of menstruation after the first menstruation, because the ruling for such a woman is that she counts that one menstruation and then two months after it. And if the woman is one who does not menstruate except every three years or four years, her waiting period is three months.
ai.seo_question: How is the waiting period calculated for a woman with irregular or infrequent menstruation after divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the fiqh of *iddah* for women with irregular menstruation (*al-mustahadhdah*), distinguishing between those with extended but regular cycles and those entering menopause (*al-mustahadhdah al-kubra*). The text demonstrates the Shia scholarly method of reconciling variant narrations by contextualizing the 'one period' report as applicable to women who have ceased menstruating, thereby establishing a three-month waiting period for those with triennial cycles. This ruling underscores the practical application of Quranic principles to unique physiological states, ensuring legal clarity for remarriage.
